A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Multimodal RewardBench 2 and provide complete 45-page manuscripts, including figures, tables and Appendices A–E. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison; all appendix pages are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-preference data, reward-model evaluations, downstream best-of-N experiments and diagnostic analyses in Section 4, with additional results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical studies, including judge accuracies, downstream correlations, test-time scaling results and generation win rates.

M1.justification: The ensemble filtering, annotation and pair-construction procedures, positional dual evaluation and generation agents are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices B–C. The newly discussed methods belong to related work.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same four benchmark tasks, 21 prompt sources and represented scenarios. Downstream evaluation still uses GenAI-Bench, GEdit-Bench, ISG-Bench and EMMA.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and appendix experiments. The added references to LLaVA-Critic, EvalPlanner, J1, DSG and OmniVerifier are related-work citations, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both versions retain 1,000 preference pairs per task, the same annotation and filtering rules, dual-order judging and evaluator-specific subsets. Best-of-N sampling still uses N=8, and the scaling study retains 300 examples per task and the same K values.

E4.justification: The downstream correlation study, same-model versus different-model analysis, modality-bias analysis and test-time scaling study are unchanged. Appendix A's supplementary analyses and Appendix E's examples are also retained without additions.

E5.justification: Statistical and repetition reporting is unchanged, including Figure 4's correlation displays and Section 4.5's independent-judgment sampling description. No new seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains average accuracies of 76.3% for Gemini 3 Pro, 72.2% for GPT-5 and 64.6% for Qwen3-VL-32B.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised. The agreement definition in Section 3.4 and win-rate definition in Appendix A.2 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and claims about judge limitations, human agreement gaps and downstream predictive value. The related-work additions do not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning reasoning difficulty, modality bias and possible distribution shift are unchanged. Section 5 and Appendix D retain the same applicability boundaries and limitations concerning modalities, task formats, data coverage and preference dimensions.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C retain identical annotation instructions, prompts, tool definitions, generation defaults and agent limits. The code and data access statement is unchanged, with no additional implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds LLaVA-Critic, LLaVA-Critic-R1, EvalPlanner, J1, DSG and OmniVerifier, broadening discussion of trained judges, test-time scaling and visual verification. This is a localized literature expansion; the paper's central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in one expanded Related Work paragraph, a spelling correction and date/version updates. The section structure is preserved. The new OmniVerifier sentence introduces a visibly corrupted word where 'models' is intended.

P2.justification: Table 2 moves from page 7 to page 8, and Table 3 becomes wider with single-line column headings. Other changes mainly concern local text and reference reflow; figures are retained and appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: The expanded Related Work gives readers more complete context for learned multimodal critics, reasoning-based judges and visual verification, modestly improving attribution and positioning. Scientific evidence and reproducibility remain unchanged. The corrupted word in the new OmniVerifier sentence reduces polish, but this localized defect does not outweigh the limited contextual benefit.
